subject: QBR orbit: OKR checkpoint + launch timeline risk scan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QBR orbit: OKR checkpoint + launch timeline risk scan

Team —

We have the executive QBR in two weeks. For the product/engineering segment I want a compact run-rate overview and a short risk-scan tied to the launch timelines for the next two releases. Please keep inputs tight — one slide equivalent per owner. Specifically: 

- OKR status: health (on-track / behind / blocked) and two-line reason for current status.
- Launch timelines: committed dates, hard cut dates, and rollback windows. Call out any single-point-of-failure owners.
- Delivery risks: top 3 risks per area with mitigations and expected ETA for mitigation.

Deliverables: 
- One consolidated OKRs snapshot (PDF) — attach to this thread.
- Staging risk matrix (spreadsheet) with severity and owner.
- One action item list with owners and dates for any untriaged risks.

Please send your sections by EOD Friday PST so I can synthesize for the Monday QBR pack. If you foresee needing more runway for any customer-facing commitments (Acme integrator, DEAL-4372), call it out now so we can surface to GTM.

Thanks —
Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Product
Redwood Inference

Attachments: okrs-briefing-2028Q2.pdf (draft), staging-risk-matrix.xlsx (template)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 May 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QBR orbit: OKR checkpoint + launch timeline risk scan

Thanks Marissa — short summary from Eng below. I kept this to the three asks and an explicit owner list.

OKR health (eng):
- Model-serving reliability (OKR 1.2): At risk — memory regression observed in nightly KV-cache runs (blame: recent attention kernel patch). Owner: Jonas Weber (infra). Mitigation: revert kernel in staging + cold-cache run; ETA: 72h.
- Latency SLO for small payloads (OKR 2.1): On-track — micro-batching improvements rolling out; ETA for full rollout: next week. Owner: Aditya Rao.
- Cost/unit reduction (OKR 3.1): Behind — quantized 4-bit rollout slowed by fidelity regressions on reranking tests. Owner: Monica Patel. Mitigation: canary variant with fallback to 8-bit; ETA: 10 business days.

Launch timeline implications:
- Release 2028-05-18 (internal beta): at risk if KV-cache regression not mitigated by 2028-05-07. If not fixed, fallback plan: disable cache priming for two endpoints (15% throughput impact) to preserve correctness. Owner: Jonas (decision), Monica (ops).
- Release 2028-06-08 (customer-facing): contingent on quantization canary health. If canary fails, propose rolling customer launch to 2028-06-22. Owner: Aditya (ship), Marissa (go/no-go).

Top delivery risks (eng view):
1) KV-cache memory regression (high) — mitigation: rollback kernel + extended staging validation (72h).
2) Quantization fidelity on rerank models (high) — mitigation: A/B canary + automated evals; holdback if regressions >2% in IR metrics.
3) Infra autoscaler flapping under burst (medium) — mitigation: temporary headroom in Dedicated pool + autoscaler threshold tweak.

Action items:
- Jonas to post rollback plan w/ runbook by EOD today.
- Monica to populate staging-risk-matrix.xlsx with severity and owners by noon.
- Aditya to prepare a customer communication template if we need to shift 2028-06-08.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
CTO, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: QBR orbit: OKR checkpoint + launch timeline risk scan

Uploading the staging-risk-matrix.xlsx with current entries — attaching here. Quick notes from Ops: 

- KV-cache regression: reproduced on three staging runs. Root cause appears tied to the fused-attention kernel change when sequences exceed 2.5k tokens. Immediate mitigation: pin kernel to previous release for the affected pool and run a targeted memory profile. Owner: Jonas. ETA for profile and decision: 48 hours.
- Quantization canary: we have one customer canary running (internal name: q-canary-17). Observed reranking drift in 2 of 25 test prompts; severity is medium-high because it impacts ranking-sensitive flows. Proposal: expand canary to 5% of traffic and add automated IR checks; rollout gating next review 2028-05-11. Owner: Monica.
- Autoscaler flapping: correlated with a sudden spike in scheduled batch jobs. Temporary mitigation: suppress scheduled test bursts during the 05-05 to 05-09 window and add a throttle. Owner: SRE oncall; ETA: 24h.

Scheduling: I recommend a focused 30-minute pre-QBR engineering/product sync Monday 08:30 PST to finalize the slide and action owners. Marissa — can your team host the doc/synth if we get inputs Friday EOD?

Attachments: staging-risk-matrix.xlsx (see sheet 'severity_by_area')

—Monica
Monica Patel
Director, Engineering Operations
Redwood Inference

2) SOW update: procurement flagged that the quantization rollout and any feature-flag-induced performance differences need to be documented in an SOW addendum. Natalie is copied for procurement coordination.

If there's time in the pre-QBR sync Monday, we'd like a 10-minute slot to confirm integration acceptance criteria. Otherwise we can do a separate 15-minute call early next week.
